source.description: A right-of-center national outlet's account of the charges, included to show how the incident was covered outside regional media; walks through the video timeline showing Borrenpohl asking guards to identify themselves before being pulled to the ground.

source.title: Spokane plans to create its own 911 system, separate from SREC
source.section: Spokane's Split from Regional 911 Dispatch (SREC)
source.description: The city and Spokane Regional Emergency Communications head to mediation after the city says SREC has been “disagreeable and unwilling” to accommodate its needs; Mayor Lisa Brown credits a new state law, HB 1258, with ensuring a fairer split of 911 excise-tax funding if the city must build its own system.

source.title: Spokane regional 911 service taps AI system to route non-emergency dispatch calls
source.section: Spokane's Split from Regional 911 Dispatch (SREC)
source.description: SREC contracts with Prepared AI, working with body-camera maker Axon, to triage the roughly 250,000 annual nonemergency Crime Check calls — nearly half of which don't involve a crime — for $95,000 a year; the AI will not handle actual 911 emergencies, and the sheriff says he was initially skeptical but became convinced after testing.

source.title: Agreement gives Spokane two years to fully transition away from regional 911, avoids 'potential crisis'
source.section: Spokane's Split from Regional 911 Dispatch (SREC)
source.description: With days to spare before SREC's deadline to expel the city, Spokane, the county, and SREC strike a phased three-step handover running through January 2028, splitting 911 excise-tax funding by population share in the interim rather than the disputed call-volume formula the city had sought.

source.title: 'Disagreeable and unwilling'; City, SREC end negotiations for regionalization
source.section: Spokane's Split from Regional 911 Dispatch (SREC)
source.description: The SREC board of directors formally ends years of talks aimed at folding Spokane fully into the regional dispatch system, an early step in the standoff that eventually forced the 2025 mediation and transition agreement.

source.title: SREC terminates contract with Spokane Fire, city now has six months for new 911 service
source.section: Spokane's Split from Regional 911 Dispatch (SREC)
source.description: SREC formally terminates its dispatch contract with the Spokane Fire Department, an earlier flashpoint in the multiyear dispute that predates the 2025 mediation and eventual phased-transition deal.

source.title: Baumgartner calls on Zelenskyy to resign hours after diplomatic meltdown in Oval Office
source.section: Additional Regional Politics and Accountability Stories
source.description: After a televised Oval Office clash between Trump, Vance, and Zelenskyy over a Ukraine minerals deal, Baumgartner calls for Ukraine's president to step down; a WSU political-science professor calls the congressman's position “shameful” and the administration's conduct “disgraceful.”

source.title: Federal workers across the Northwest are being fired by the Trump administration. They warn of impacts to wildfires, science and historic landmarks
source.section: Additional Regional Politics and Accountability Stories
source.description: Mass probationary firings hit roughly 3,400 USDA employees regionally, including a Palouse crop researcher and a Mount St. Helens lead park ranger; a Forest Service union official warns the cuts strip away dispatchers and support staff who backstop wildland firefighters just before fire season.

source.title: Former Spokane police officer awaiting trial for rape charges arrested again for allegedly raping another woman
source.section: Additional Regional Politics and Accountability Stories
source.description: Nathan Nash, fired by SPD in 2019 after a domestic-violence victim accused him of assaulting her during a follow-up visit, is arrested on a second rape charge after another woman comes forward; both accusers say Nash exploited his uniform and position to isolate them, and a supervisor's internal review of the underlying 2019 incident had earlier come under separate scrutiny.

source.title: Spokane City Council condemns attacks in Israel
source.section: Additional Regional Politics and Accountability Stories
source.description: The council votes unanimously to condemn Hamas's attacks, affirm Israel's right to “exist and defend itself,” and voice support for both Jewish and Palestinian Spokane residents; sponsor Jonathan Bingle says he modeled the resolution on the council's earlier statement of solidarity with Ukraine.

source.title: Watching the watchmen
source.section: Flock Cameras, License Plate Readers, and Mass Surveillance
source.description: The editor's-note launch of RANGE's Flock investigation reveals that in just the first half of 2025, outside agencies searched Spokane County's license-plate database more than 2.3 million times — over 95% of all searches — including from Texas and Alabama, states actively prosecuting abortion-related travel, despite Washington law barring local police from aiding federal immigration enforcement.

source.title: Texas deputy searched Spokane County Flock cameras for a woman who had an abortion
source.section: Flock Cameras, License Plate Readers, and Mass Surveillance
source.description: Records show a Texas officer's search of Spokane's camera network listed “had an abortion, search for female” as the justification; RANGE's review finds over 289,000 searches logged with no case number and only a generic “investigation” reason, none of which complied with the sheriff's office's own written search policy.

source.title: Protested this year? Cops might've looked for you on Flock cams
source.section: Flock Cameras, License Plate Readers, and Mass Surveillance
source.description: Published with data analysis from the University of Washington's Center for Human Rights, the story finds Spokane County deputies made 24 searches for vehicles tied to 2025 protests, including an SPD officer who searched 197 cameras across eight networks for a car spotted near a 'March for Liberty' demonstration.

source.title: 'Operation Pimp Juice,' 'Serial Beer Thief,' and Grand Theft Excavator
source.section: Flock Cameras, License Plate Readers, and Mass Surveillance
source.description: A lighter entry in the same investigative series catalogs oddly named or vaguely justified searches of Spokane's camera network by outside agencies, including a Florida officer's search reason that read simply “theft from a Publix,” contrasted against the Sheriff's Office's own marketing claims about cameras helping recover stolen vehicles.

source.title: Happy holidays! Here's all our Flock data
source.section: Flock Cameras, License Plate Readers, and Mass Surveillance
source.description: RANGE publishes the raw camera-search datasets underlying its investigation along with a public-records request guide, describing a four-month wait between its original request and the Sheriff's Office's first records production.

source.title: Flock-enheit 451
source.section: Flock Cameras, License Plate Readers, and Mass Surveillance
source.description: An opinion column arguing that Flock's ever-expanding camera network erodes a meaningful expectation of privacy in public space, and pointing readers toward the ACLU, the Electronic Frontier Foundation, and the outlet 404 Media for further reporting and advocacy on automated license-plate-reader surveillance.

word_cloud.note: Frequency-weighted terms computed from all source titles and descriptions; used to render the term-frequency visualization on the webpage.
